findings.body:
**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

This frontmatter rewrites the router as **four** capabilities and drops `apply-review`, while also setting `version: "1.6.2"`. On `main` (`ref: base`) the same fields are **five** capabilities including apply-review and `version: "2.5.1"`. Merging this branch as written would publish a stale skill contract: agents stop routing “what did the CI review say?” / “apply the AI review’s fixes” to the apply-review sub-skill, and the shipped skill version jumps backward. Rebase onto current `main` and re-apply only the narrative edits on top of the five-capability text.

**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

The capabilities table stops at `#4 open-pr` under “**Four** coordinated capabilities”. On `main` this is “**Five** coordinated capabilities” with row `#5 apply-review` (`☁️ CI → 🖥️ Local`). That row is how dual-surface consumers close the loop after CI posts findings; removing it is a product-surface regression, not a docs polish. Restore row 5 (and the Five/four wording) when rebasing.

Version-parity guidance tells consumers that pinning `@v1.4.2` on both surfaces “guarantees identical reviews”. Current `main` pins `@v2.1.0` and explicitly notes IAR may shorten CI round-2+ finding sets vs a local full pass. Shipping the v1.4.2 pin misdirects Marketplace/skill consumers onto an obsolete major and overstates local↔CI identity. Use the current major pin and keep the IAR caveat from `main`.

Install examples say “Latest **v1.x**” and `npx skills add …@v1.4.2`. On `main` the same block is “Latest **v2.x**” / `@v2.1.0`. Copy-paste from this skill would pin consumers to the old major after the v2 line is current. Update the comments and pin to the live major when rebasing.

**Claimed critical; verifier found:** verifier off

The new “Default flow” header says Steps 0–5 cover only capability #1 and lists **three** sibling sub-skills (`generate-extension`, `setup`, `open-pr`). On `main` the same section lists **four** siblings and includes [`apply-review/SKILL.md`](apply-review/SKILL.md). Dropping that pointer orphans the apply-review flow from the parent skill’s navigation even if the sub-skill directory still exists on `main`. Restore the fourth bullet (and “four sibling sub-skills”) after rebase.

summary:
I'd recommend not merging until this branch is rebased onto current `main` — as written it regresses the parent skill from the live five-capability / v2.x contract back to a four-capability / v1.6.x snapshot.

## What went wrong

The PR description frames this as a pure narrative reframe of an older “Local Companion” opening, with Steps 0–5 left byte-identical. Against the review base (`main` @ `38c6144`), that is not what the head tree contains:

| Surface | `main` (base) | This branch (head) |
|---|---|---|
| Frontmatter `version` | `2.5.1` | `1.6.2` |
| Capabilities | **Five**, including `apply-review` | **Four**, stops at `open-pr` |
| Install pin | `Latest v2.x` / `@v2.1.0` | `Latest v1.x` / `@v1.4.2` |
| Default-flow siblings | four (`…` + `apply-review`) | three |
| CI-only surfaces (IAR / skip-review-label / follow-up) | present | absent from the rewritten intro/flows area |

`skills/ai-diff-reviewer/apply-review/SKILL.md` exists on base as a first-class sub-skill; the head worktree under review has no `apply-review/` path at all. Merging this branch would therefore not only mis-document the router — it would publish a skill package that no longer routes “what did the CI review say?” / “apply the AI review’s fixes” and would teach consumers obsolete `@v1.4.2` pins.

The intended editorial wins (Two audiences frame, Surface column, flows-before-install order, explicit Default-flow header) are still worth doing — but only as a rebase of those edits onto current `main`, preserving five capabilities, v2 pins, apply-review activation/triggers, and the CI-only surfaces section.

## Also missing vs main (not all re-posted inline)

Beyond the five anchored findings: Flow A/B rows no longer mention `apply-review`; Activation lost the apply-review trigger block and the PR-marker disambiguation heuristic; the Parity paragraph lost the IAR “shorter on round 2+” caveat. Treat those as part of the same stale-base fix rather than separate nits.
